entry.evidence: the drivers of surface seawater carbonate system variability in the areas affected by the ITCZ in the tropical Atlantic have not been addressed to date

sequences.source_document: Published PDF (Science of the Total Environment 838, 156592), with publisher XML for the abstract and captions

steps.action: Posed the aim: evaluate how intense ITCZ rainfall affects fCO2sw and sea-air CO2 fluxes in the tropical Atlantic, and disentangle the drivers by comparing observed fCO2sw with thermodynamic expectation.
steps.quote: The main objective of this study is therefore to evaluate the impact of the intense rainfall associated with the [...]

steps.action: Used underway fCO2sw, fCO2atm, SST, SSS and pressure recorded by an autonomous LI-COR system and thermosalinograph on commercial ships, on 35 crossings between 5°S and 15°N, 2008–2014. The data come from a routine monitoring line curated by a co-author and published as SEANOE datasets.
steps.quote: Data used were collected between 15°N and 5°S (Lefèvre and Diverrès, 2021a,b) from 35 voyages

steps.action: Replaced missing shipboard atmospheric xCO2 (March–April 2011) with interpolated NOAA station data, and checked the procedure against tracks with measured fCO2atm (mean deviation 1.70 μatm, within instrument precision).
steps.quote: Comparison of both calculated and measured fCO2atm gives very good results, with deviations (average 1.70 μatm, n = 40,925; see Supplementary materials)

steps.action: Interpolated external remote-sensed and reanalysis products to the ship tracks: ERA-interim wind, TRMM rainfall, OSCAR currents, MODIS Chl a, MERRA-2 wet and dry dust deposition, and SMOS SSS.
steps.quote: Daily rainfall data are obtained from the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM)

steps.action: Found the naturally occurring conditions. Areas affected by recent rain were selected with a 4-day accumulated TRMM rainfall threshold of 1 mm, and water masses were separated into SEC, NECC and NEC using the zonal velocity of monthly OSCAR currents.
steps.quote: An accumulated rainfall threshold of 1 mm is used to discern among areas affected and not affected by recent rainfall.

steps.action: Varied the arbitrary 4-day rainfall integration period by ±2 days and reported highly similar results (data not shown).
steps.quote: This arbitrary integration time-period was varied (±2 days) offering highly similar results ( [...] ).

steps.action: Tested the reanalysis and remote-sensed wind, rainfall and surface currents against PIRATA mooring measurements for 2008–2014 and found very good agreement.
steps.quote: Both sets of data showed very good agreement for the 2008–2014 period (see Supplementary materials).

steps.action: Took the thermodynamic expectations from the literature: the Takahashi temperature coefficient, and a dilution sensitivity γrain ≈ 1.6 at low latitudes (Sarmiento and Gruber). Set up the per-voyage calculation of γDIC and γTAlk with CO2SYS and a TAlk–SSS relation.
steps.quote: Reported globally averaged values of γrain range from 1.6 at low latitudes to 1.7 at high latitudes

steps.action: Established from the latitudinal sections that underway SSS minima coincide with recent rainfall and follow the seasonal migration of the ITCZ.
steps.quote: The location of measured underway SSS minima almost perfectly matches the areas affected by short-term rainfall, thus following the seasonal displacement of the ITCZ

steps.action: Described ΔfCO2 by current: the SEC is a permanent source except under recent rain, the NECC is undersaturated in June–November, and the NEC is seasonally a sink or a source.
steps.quote: the waters transported by this current are a permanent source of CO2 to the atmosphere

steps.action: After normalizing fCO2sw to mean SST, regressed ln fCO2swnorm on ln SSS in rain-affected areas. Significant fits were found in 33 of 35 voyages, giving observed γrain from 1.25 to 4.98 (mean 3.12).
steps.quote: we found robust, highly significant linear relationships of ln fCO2swnorm vs ln SSS (r > 0.79, n from 217 to 837)

steps.action: Computed the thermodynamic γrain expected for each voyage from γs, γDIC (Revelle factor) and γTAlk using CO2SYS, which gave 1.58–1.60.
steps.quote: The resulting theoretical γrain calculated from γs, γDIC and γTAlk (Eq. (9)) remain systematically in the range of 1.58–1.60

steps.action: Compared the observed γrain with the thermodynamic expectation. All except two voyages (February and April 2009) were well above 1.6.
steps.quote: cannot be explained solely by thermodynamics and chemical dilution of surface waters

steps.action: Decomposed the sea-air flux into an oceanic reference part (highest SSS as the conservative reference), an ITCZ part (including rain-enhanced gas transfer) and an unexplained part, giving ITCZ-associated drawdown rates per voyage and current.
steps.quote: CO2 fluxes attributed to the impact of rainfall associated with the ITCZ range from −0.11 ± 0.01 mmol m−2 d−1

steps.action: Regressed the unexplained drawdown on the total ITCZ drawdown (R = 0.91) to estimate the average unexplained share at 59.1 ± 4.1 %.
steps.quote: 59.1 ± 4.1 % of the total observed CO2 drawdown associated with the ITCZ cannot be explained by abiotic processes.

steps.action: Rejected a purely abiotic account (SSS change, dilution of DIC and TAlk, gas transfer) as sufficient, since it explains only about 41 % of the drawdown.
steps.quote: abiotic factors (SSS changes and DIC and TAlk dilution caused by rainfall) only explain ~41 % of the calculated CO2 drawdown

steps.action: Correlated monthly MODIS Chl a interpolated to the tracks with underway SSS and fCO2swnorm, finding significant negative correlations in most rain-affected areas.
steps.quote: we find significant negative correlations between monthly Chl a and underway SSS in the majority of the areas

steps.action: Took up the Pacific hypothesis of Hansell and Feely: rain-induced stratification under N limitation favours diazotrophs and lowers fCO2sw.
steps.quote: In the Pacific Ocean, Hansell and Feely (2000) hypothesize that increased stratification forced by rainfall associated with the ITCZ

steps.action: Converted the unexplained drawdown into the N2 fixation it would imply, using a cultured Trichodesmium CO2:N2 ratio of 28 (median 13.0 μmol m−2 d−1).
steps.quote: would represent N2fixation ratios ranging from 2.2 ± 0.2 to 53.9 ± 1.9 μmol m−2 d−1

steps.action: Compared the implied N2 fixation rates with published field measurements in the region (Fernández et al. 2010 and others) and found them within the measured range.
steps.quote: These potential N2 fixation ratios calculated are well within the range of values previously measured in the studied area.

steps.action: Proposed that the ITCZ supports primary production through wet deposition of African dust, which fertilizes the oligotrophic tropical Atlantic.
steps.quote: suggest a direct link between the ITCZ and primary production in the central tropical Atlantic

steps.action: Mapped the MERRA-2 dust deposition climatology and its anomalies. Wet deposition exceeds dry deposition by an order of magnitude, peaks just north of the ITCZ and varies between years.
steps.quote: wet dust deposition is the main pathway of entrance of Saharan and Sahel dust to surface waters

steps.action: Correlated the ITCZ CO2 drawdown with monthly wet dust deposition anomalies in the SEC (ρ = 0.41, p < 0.05, n = 28) rather than with rainfall anomalies.
steps.quote: calculated CO2 drawdown associated with the ITCZ showed significant correlation with monthly wet dust deposition anomalies in the SEC

steps.action: Recomputed monthly-averaged drawdown from monthly wind and rainfall fields and found it still correlated with wet dust anomalies (ρ = 0.35, n = 44).
steps.quote: monthly-averaged CO2 drawdown associated with the ITCZ, calculated using the monthly-averaged wind and rainfall fields, showed also significant correlation

steps.action: Checked the shape of the ln SSS vs ln fCO2swnorm relations. The steeper slopes at higher SSS are consistent with stronger dust deposition at the northern edge of the ITCZ.
steps.quote: This is consistent with higher wet dust deposition at the northern edge of the ITCZ.

steps.action: Computed Ekman pumping at 5°S, 7.5°N and 12.5°N and set aside upwelling of nutrient- and CO2-rich water as the main contributor. Downwelling prevails in the SEC, and no CO2 increase is observed under the ITCZ (Bruto et al. 2017).
steps.quote: vertical Ekman transport may not be the main contributor to the observed enhanced Chl a

steps.action: Derived the salinity sensitivity expected from Amazon plume mixing (1.67 ± 0.06) from the authors' earlier fCO2–SSS relation for the outer plume.
steps.quote: the overall effect of salinity changes caused by the plume over fCO2sw is 1.67 ± 0.06

steps.action: Rejected Amazon plume mixing as the explanation for the enhanced drawdown in the NECC, because its sensitivity is much smaller than the observed γrain; some contribution is not ruled out.
steps.quote: it cannot explain the enhanced CO2 drawdown observed

steps.action: Qualified the flux estimates as conservative, because the 3–5 m ship intake likely misses the shallow freshened layer. Cautioned against basin-scale extrapolation given east–west gradients in dust and river plumes.
steps.quote: our findings can be taken as a conservative estimation of the impact of the ITCZ over the sea-air CO2 exchange

steps.action: Kept the claim that ITCZ-driven dust fertilization enhances primary production and is the main mechanism behind the large CO2 drawdown.
steps.quote: These, in turn, fertilize the oligotrophic tropical Atlantic and seem to be the main mechanism explaining the large CO2 drawdown caused by the ITCZ.

end.claim: ITCZ-driven fertilization, mainly through wet deposition of African dust, seems to enhance primary production in the oligotrophic tropical Atlantic and to explain the CO2 drawdown beyond thermodynamics, significantly lowering CO2 emissions.

decisive_move.sentence: Without comparing the observed γrain from the per-voyage regressions with the thermodynamic γrain of about 1.6, there would be no unexplained drawdown to attribute to biology.

gates.evidence: The data came from a routine VOS monitoring line, not collected under a stated hypothesis (p. 2). The thermodynamic account faced a test it could have passed: the observed γrain could have matched 1.58–1.60 (p. 9). The biological claim rests on correlations with monthly Chl a and dust anomalies (ρ = 0.41) and on plausibility against published N2 fixation rates, so it was not exposed to a decisive test (pp. 10–11). The 1.6 benchmark was published beforehand (Sarmiento and Gruber 2006), but the analysis choices (1 mm threshold, 4-day window, highest-SSS reference) were set by the authors, two of them called arbitrary, with nothing registered (pp. 3–6).

imports.item: CO2:N2 utilization ratio of 28 from cultured Trichodesmium IMS101 (Mulholland and Capone 2001), used to convert drawdown into implied N2 fixation
High iron cost of the nitrogenase enzyme, so that diazotrophs are iron-limited
Linear regression and correlation significance tests (Pearson r, rank ρ, p-values) across voyages

novelty_claims.quote: the drivers of surface seawater carbonate system variability in the areas affected by the ITCZ in the tropical Atlantic have not been addressed to date
we show evidence for the enhanced CO2 drawdown associated with the ITCZ in the tropical Atlantic

limits: Locators: the XML supplied holds only the abstract and captions, so body text is cited by printed pages (identical to PDF pages). The Supplementary materials cited for the fCO2atm and PIRATA checks and for the fCO2sw differences between currents were not supplied. No review file was supplied; the paper thanks three anonymous reviewers and was revised (received 11 January 2022, revised 14 May 2022), but what changed is unknown, so there is no review sequence. Coding the VOS data as 'inherited' is an inference: a co-author ran the monitoring line and published it as SEANOE datasets, and the paper does not say whether acquisition was part of this study. Sub-claims and their statuses: the ITCZ-associated drawdown rates of 0.11–2.35 mmol m−2 d−1 are estimate_with_resolution (pp. 9–10); the 59.1 ± 4.1 % unexplained share is estimate_with_resolution (§0 ¶1); the exclusion of a purely thermodynamic account is the firmest result (p. 9); the dust-fertilization mechanism is best_explanation only, resting on monthly-satellite and reanalysis correlations without in situ biological or nutrient measurements. The Amazon plume contribution 'cannot be disregarded' (p. 13), and Ekman transport is downgraded rather than excluded. Internal inconsistencies: the abstract gives the minimum drawdown as 0.11 ± 0.02 while the text gives −0.11 ± 0.01 (p. 9); the text places that minimum in 'May 2013', whereas Table 3 lists it for voyage 33 in April 2013. The ±2-day sensitivity is reported only as 'data not shown'. The highest-SSS reference for oceanic waters is called conservative, but no alternative reference is tested. The inferred N2 fixation assumes a culture stoichiometry for natural populations.

disagreements.target: Ho and Schanze (2020); Turk et al. (2010): rainfall effects on fCO2sw in the tropical Pacific explained by physics and [...]
disagreements.support: In the tropical Atlantic the observed γrain (mean 3.12) far exceeds the thermodynamic 1.58–1.60, which the paper attributes to Atlantic particularities (dust, river plumes).
disagreements.quote: the physical and thermodynamic effects of rainfall over the carbonate system successfully explained the observed fCO2sw

disagreements.target: Sarmiento and Gruber (2006): global low-latitude γrain ≈ 1.6
disagreements.support: Per-voyage regressions give γrain of 1.25–4.98, nearly all well above 1.6, although CO2SYS calculations reproduce 1.6 thermodynamically.
disagreements.quote: all the remaining γrain are well above the γrain reported from global means of the carbonate system sensitivity to rainfall at low latitudes

disagreements.target: Ashton et al. (2016): rainfall causing up to 6 % of the global oceanic CO2 sink
disagreements.support: The paper argues that underway-based estimates include rain effects without attributing them, so changes in the precipitation regime would alter the sink unquantified.
disagreements.quote: the effect of rainfall over the sea surface carbonate system is already accounted in their estimations but not directly attributed to rainfall
